newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar, Britain discuss arms deal financing.
newsitem.headline: Qatar, Britain discuss arms deal financing.

text.p: Qatar and Britain are discussing setting up a revolving credit package to finance an $825 million arms deal signed in November, a British minister said on Sunday.

Asked if the two countries were discussing a revolving credit facility for the deal, Britain's Defence Procurement Minister James Arbuthnot said "Yes, there is a financial instrument involved in the deal".

"It is an extremely complicated arrangement, indeed, related to what equipment will delivered and when. Details have still to be completely concluded. But discussions are going well and we are satisfied," he told a news conference.
Arbuthnot declined to disclose details. But informed sources said a portion of the contract might be paid in crude oil.

Qatar and Britain signed the deal in Doha in November. It involves GKN Pirhanha armoured personnel carriers, Vosper Thornycroft patrol boats, British Aerospace Hawk training aircraft, and Starburst missiles by Short Missile Systems, a joint venture between Short Brothers and France's Thomson-CSF. Western diplomats and industry experts said the package will help Britain recover lost ground in the Gulf, where leading weapons makers are in fierce competition to sell their latest high-tech weaponry to oil-rich cutomers.

The United States, France and Britain all have defence pacts with Qatar, whose natural gas reserves -- the world's third largest -- make it one of the most strategic sources of clean energy in the next century.
